question: Further to my previous question on violations of EU law in the trade and import of used goods vehicles from Member States1, it should again be noted that Greek legislation imposes less favourable rules on and discriminates against the import and registration of these commercial goods, creating significant obstacles and quantitative restrictions for intra-Community trade2.

In particular, new public use licences can only be issued for goods vehicles in the Euro 6d category3, ruling out a significant portion of the used vehicle fleet available in the EU. At the same time, the high price of the few used vehicles that are available on the EU market leads to the less favourable and unequal treatment of importers of such vehicles compared to traders of new or domestic used good vehicles.

What is more, the unjustified amount of red tape created by the new digital register (MEMO)4, together with the requirement for an additional roadworthiness certificate in the vehicle’s country of origin – in addition to the domestic inspection required at registration in Greece – as well as the obligation to issue and submit a certificate of conformity at disproportionately high costs, result in additional unjustified obstacles and delays for importers.
This discrimination is harmful to the environment and intra-Community trade. It also shrinks the sector and promotes the recycling of the old fleet rather than its renewal5. In view of the above: 1.
Has the Commission assessed whether these rules violate EU legislation and discriminate against importers of used goods vehicles?
What action will it take to ensure Greece’s compliance with EU law?
See: E-001076/2024 https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-9-2024-001076_EN.html Specifically, the implementation of this legislation violates Article 34 et seq. TFEU.

See CJEU judgments C112/00 - Schmidberger, EU:C:2003:333, paragraph 56, C-110/05 - Commission v Italy (2009), ECLI:EU:C:2009:66, paragraph 56, C-297/05 - Commission v Netherlands (2007), ECLI:EU:C:2007:531, paragraph 63 and 4/75 and ECLI:EU:C:1975:98. Essentially, vehicles manufactured from 2020 onwards. Categories N1, N2 and N3, O1, O2 and O3.The harmful rules concern all heavy duty vehicles (public and private).

The obligation to register data on new imported used goods vehicles in MEMO is imposed only on importers of used goods vehicles and not on traders of already registered used goods vehicles in Greece. They must upload a number of supporting documents within 20 days of registering a vehicle in Greece, which they had already provided at the time of the vehicle’s registration.
According to ACEA, Greece’s fleet of goods vehicles and buses is the oldest in the EU.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.2.2025) The Commission has assessed the Greek legislation imposing new rules for imported used vehicles in Greece.

Provided that the new licencing procedure is applicable for all used heavy-duty vehicles, domestic or imported, and is thus non-discriminatory, the choice of the environmental standard EURO 6D as a condition for granting the permission to perform public transport services is regulated under national law and does not appear to be in breach of EU law.

From a general point of view, where a second-hand (used) vehicle is imported from another Member State and is covered by an EU type-approval issued pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2018/8581, the authorities of the Member States must recognise the vehicle approval and the registration certificate, without carrying out additional checks2.

A Member State does not have discretion not to recognise such a vehicle, save in specific cases where there is a presumption of fraud or alteration; without however duplicating controls which have been carried out in the context of other procedures, either in the same or in another Member State.

Member States must duly justify any additional requirements for the registration of an imported vehicle from another Member State in a (new) dedicated domestic register, for the electronic submission of a number of documents within a limited period of time from the date of the application, or for the provision of additional roadworthiness certificate, and/or a copy of the certificate of conformity of the vehicle, at a certain cost.
Addition requirements shall be limited to cases where such controls are necessary and proportionate to the objective pursued.
1 Regulation (EU) 2018/858 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May 2018 on the approval and

market surveillance of motor vehicles and their trailers, and of systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, amending Regulations (EC) No 715/2007 and (EC) No 595/2009 and repealing Directive 2007/46/EC, OJ L 151, 14.6.2018, p. 1-218. 2 Article 4 and Article 5(2) of Council Directive 1999/37/EC of 29 April 1999 on the registration documents for vehicles, OJ L 138, 1.6.1999, p. 57-65.
